name: telegram-call
author: Keith Yeung
description: Synthesizes spoken audio from text via a local Kokoro-FastAPI server and places a 1-on-1 Telegram voice call that plays it. Self-installs and self-authenticates on first use; auth has a dedicated verification tool so a wrong code can be retried without invalidating it.

tools.name: synthesize_speech
tools.description: Convert a text message into an mp3 audio file using a local Kokoro-FastAPI server (default http://localhost:8880, override via KOKORO_URL env). Returns the absolute path of the generated audio file. Use this whenever the user asks to call someone with a spoken message rather than a pre-recorded file (e.g. 'call @alice about a possible gas leak'): first call this tool with the spoken text, then pass the returned path to `make_call` as `audio_path`. Results are cached by (voice, speed, text) hash so calling twice with the same args is free.

text.description: The message to speak. Should be a complete, natural-sounding spoken message — write it the way you'd say it out loud. Example: 'Hi Alice, this is an automated alert. There may be a gas leak in your house. Please check immediately and call emergency services if you smell gas.'

voice.description: Optional Kokoro voice name (e.g. 'af_heart', 'af_bella', 'af_nova', 'am_michael', 'bf_emma', 'bm_george'). Defaults to 'af_heart' or the KOKORO_VOICE env var.

speed.description: Optional speech rate multiplier (1.0 = normal, 0.5 = slow, 1.5 = fast). Defaults to 1.0.

tools.name: verify_telegram_code
tools.description: Submit a Telegram verification code (or 2FA cloud password) during the one-time login flow. ONLY use this AFTER `make_call` returned a message asking for a code or password — never as the first step. The tool figures out from internal state whether to verify a `code` or a `password`; pass whichever one the user supplied. NOTE on where the code comes from: when Telegram issues a login code it is delivered as an in-app message from the official 'Telegram' service account to the user's existing logged-in Telegram sessions (their phone app, Telegram Desktop, etc.); SMS is a slow fallback that may take a minute or more, or fail silently on some carriers. If the user says they 'didn't get a code', tell them to check the 'Telegram' chat in their app first. If Telegram rejects the value as invalid (a typo), the auth state is preserved so you can retry by calling this tool again with a corrected value — do NOT call `make_call` with `phone` again, that would invalidate the code that was already sent. After this tool succeeds you can call `make_call` to place the actual call.

code.description: The verification code Telegram sent to the user (typically 5 digits, no spaces or dashes). Provide this when `make_call` returned a 'verification code was sent' message.

password.description: The user's Telegram 2FA cloud password. Provide this when verification returned a '2FA enabled' message asking for `password`.

tools.name: make_call
tools.description: Place a 1-on-1 Telegram voice call to a user, play an audio file, and hang up. The very first invocation transparently sets up Python dependencies (~30-90s) and walks the user through a one-time Telegram login. IMPORTANT: there are TWO distinct phone numbers in this skill — `phone` (this parameter) is the Telegram account that PLACES the call, i.e. the user's own account; `target` is the RECIPIENT being called. They are not the same. The login flow is: (a) call `make_call` with `phone` set to the USER'S OWN Telegram number to trigger a verification code (delivered as an in-app message to their existing Telegram sessions first, SMS is a slow fallback); (b) call the SEPARATE `verify_telegram_code` tool with the `code` (and `password` if 2FA is enabled) — DO NOT call `make_call` with `phone` again after a code has been sent or you will invalidate it; (c) once verification succeeds, call `make_call` again with `target` and `audio_path` to actually place the call. If the user asked you to convey a spoken message (no pre-recorded file given), first call `synthesize_speech` to turn the text into an mp3, then pass that path here as `audio_path`. If `target` is missing, ASK the user — do not invent one.

target.description: Who to call on Telegram — i.e. the RECIPIENT. NOT the same as `phone` (which is the caller's own account during one-time auth). Accepts @username, numeric user_id, or +phone_number (phone numbers only resolve if that user is already in the caller's Telegram contacts; prefer @username when in doubt). If the user has not specified a target, ASK them rather than guessing.

audio_path.description: Absolute path to the audio file to play during the call. Any format ffmpeg can decode is accepted (mp3, wav, ogg, m4a, opus, ...). Typically obtained by first calling `synthesize_speech` with the spoken text.

message.description: Human-readable description of the call, surfaced in the success/failure output.

phone.description: ONE-TIME, FIRST-LOGIN ONLY: phone number of the Telegram account that will PLACE the call — i.e. the user's OWN Telegram account. This is NOT the recipient's phone number (the recipient is given as `target`). Use international country-code format, e.g. '+447700900000', no spaces. Only provide this on the FIRST authentication step to trigger a verification code. Do NOT include `phone` again after a code has been sent (use `verify_telegram_code` instead). Do NOT include it on normal calls once authenticated.
